native_retrieval.title: After a bear mauled him, Sitesh Ranjan Deb became a rescuer of Bangladesh’s wildlife - Butler Nature
native_retrieval.snippet: # After a bear mauled him, Sitesh Ranjan Deb became a rescuer of Bangladesh’s wildlife. * Post author    By Rhett Ayers Butler. The bear came out of the forest with enough force to kill him. During three months in a hospital, he began asking why he was hunting and killing animals. His father and grandfather were known around Sreemangal, in northeastern Bangladesh, for killing leopards, wild boars, and other animals that threatened people or crops. As a boy, Sitesh Ranjan Deb accompanied his father into the forest. The grounds of his home became a treatment center and eventually developed into the Bangladesh Wildlife Service Foundation. When a call came, he collected the animal, found room for it at home, obtained the food it needed, and worked toward the day when its cage could be carried back to the forest and opened. **Sitesh Ranjan Deb turned a hunter’s knowledge to saving wildlife**.

native_retrieval.title: Nepal, SKorea sign for USD 11.8 mn grant to boost agriculture - The Rising Nepal
native_retrieval.snippet: Photo: TRN Ghanshyam Upadhyaya, Secretary of the Ministry of Finance and Taeyoung Park, Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to Nepal after signing a MoU on Friday. **By A Staff Reporter, Kathmandu, July 25:** The government of Nepal and the Republic of Korea on Friday signed two Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) worth USD 11.8 million in grant assistance to strengthen agricultural value chains and improve public access to legal information services. Ghanshyam Upadhyaya, Secretary of the Ministry of Finance, government of Nepal and Taeyoung Park, Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to Nepal, have signed the MoU amidst a function at the Ministry of Finance. Implemented in partnership with the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, the Ministry of Government Legislation of the Republic of Korea, and the Korea Law Information Service, the project will support business process improvements, database development, essential IT infrastructure, and capacity building to enable sustainable system operation by Nepali authorities.

native_retrieval.title: FAO Director Yang calls on Agriculture Minister Chaudhary - The Rising Nepal
native_retrieval.snippet: Kathmandu, July 21: Director of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)'s South-South and Triangular Cooperation Division, Hua Yang, paid a courtesy call on Minister for Agriculture, Forests and Environment, Gita Chaudhary today. In the meeting that took place at the Ministry in Singha Durbar, they discussed food security, agricultural transformation, sustainable agriculture–food systems, development, and expanding South–South and triangular cooperation in Nepal. On the occasion, Minister Chaudhary said that Nepal is willing to further expand cooperation for transforming the agriculture sector, strengthening food security, and mobilizing international financial resources to that end. The ministry stated that during the meeting, discussions were held on cross-border animal disease control, climate-resilient agricultural development, enhancing the capacity of agricultural laboratories and establishing accredited labs, promoting the export of high-value agricultural products, and strengthening the legal and institutional arrangements related to geographical indications. Minister Chaudhary and the FAO Director on the occasion also expressed a commitment to further strengthening partnerships for sustainable, resilient, and inclusive agricultural and food system development.

english_retrieval.title: What Is the Youth-Led ‘Cockroach Movement’ Staging Mass Protests in India? - Time Magazine
english_retrieval.snippet: But it has quickly swelled into a formidable real-world political force, bringing tens of thousands of protesters into the streets in the country’s capital in recent days to call for the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and reforms to India’s troubled education system. Thousands of supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) continued to protest in the capital of New Delhi on Wednesday even after demonstrations earlier in the week erupted into violent clashes with the police that left dozens of people injured. The movement’s Monday protests in New Delhi marked one of the country’s largest anti-government gatherings in years, with an estimated 20,000 people, made up mostly of students and young people, taking to the city’s streets. Amid the massive protests, a senior government minister reportedly met with CJP representatives to hear their demands, in what was seemingly the government’s first move to hold talks with members of the movement. The following day, members of the opposition party held a protest in Parliament in support of the cockroach movement protesters.

english_retrieval.title: Police cane supporters of India’s cockroach movement as thousands gather for march - NBC News
english_retrieval.snippet: # Police cane supporters of India’s cockroach movement as thousands gather for march. The months-old movement and the planned protest are seen as the biggest public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his third term in office. NEW DELHI — Supporters of India’s youth-led “cockroach” movement were caned by police Monday as they sought to march on parliament in the capital, New Delhi, despite authorities denying permission for the protest. The months-old movement and the planned protest are seen as the biggest public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his third term in office, drawing millions of supporters on social media before broadening its appeal. A police decision to forcibly move hunger-striking activist Sonam Wangchuk to hospital on Saturday has galvanized the movement, with thousands of supporters arriving through the night at the protest site of Jantar Mantar in the heart of New Delhi for the march on the opening day of parliament’s monsoon session.
